placements.why: Shipping the async decision widget is the concrete delivery of this leaf's existing theme — the product intercepting and capturing the decision at the moment of consensus rather than letting it evaporate into scroll-back. The shipped-widget fact is evidence for this already-established narrative, not a new subject in its own right.

src-3 names the Zephyr integration — which lets decision capture embed in Slack, Teams, and Discord without separate plugins — as the causal 'key unlock', and src-2's record velocity figure is stated immediately after as its direct consequence. Read together they don't report a one-off statistic; they assert a recurring causal pattern (removing per-platform integration friction is what drives adoption/delivery velocity) that will keep recurring as the product adds integrations. This extends the existing capture-at-consensus narrative into its cross-platform delivery mechanism, but the mechanism (frictionless embedding as the velocity engine) is a distinct enough subject from 'the product captures the decision at consensus' that no existing leaf holds it directly — it names how capture reaches users, not that capture happens.
placements.title: Removing platform friction is what accelerates delivery velocity
placements.frame: Does this expression tie a velocity or adoption outcome directly to the removal of platform-specific integration friction, rather than to feature scope or raw team effort?
